title.tet: Mamíferu sira iha Timór-Leste
title.pt: Mamíferos de Timor-Leste
title.en: Mammals of Timor-Leste
title.id: Mamalia Timor-Leste

summary.tet: Mamíferu naturál sira iha Timór nia rai kuaze hotu mak niki no laho, tanba sira de'it mak bele to'o illa ho semo ka namlele iha tasi. Rusa, lekirauk, kuskus no laku mai hamutuk ho ema durante tinan rihun barak. Ohin loron mamíferu balu iha Timór iha perigu, hanesan niki ida ne'ebé ema hatene de'it iha illa ne'e.
summary.pt: Os mamíferos terrestres nativos de Timor são quase só morcegos e ratos, os únicos que conseguiram chegar à ilha a voar ou levados pelo mar. O veado, o macaco, o cusco e a civeta vieram com as pessoas ao longo de milhares de anos. Hoje alguns mamíferos de Timor estão em perigo, como um morcego que só se conhece nesta ilha.
summary.en: Timor's native land mammals are almost all bats and rats, the only ones that managed to reach the island by flying or by drifting across the sea. The deer, the macaque, the cuscus and the civet came with people over thousands of years. Today some of Timor's mammals are in danger, such as a bat known only from this island.
summary.id: Mamalia darat asli Timor hampir semuanya kelelawar dan tikus, satu-satunya yang berhasil mencapai pulau ini dengan terbang atau hanyut terbawa laut. Rusa, monyet, kuskus, dan musang datang bersama manusia selama ribuan tahun. Kini sebagian mamalia Timor terancam, misalnya satu jenis kelelawar yang hanya dikenal di pulau ini.

text.tet: Mamíferu mak animál ne'ebé dada iis, iha fulun no fó susu ba ninia oan. Ema mós mamíferu. Iha Timór-Leste iha mamíferu iha rai, iha lalehan no iha tasi: niki mak mamíferu ida de'it ne'ebé semo, no baleia, golfiñu no dugongu moris iha tasi (haree artigu kona-ba animál sira-ne'e). Maibé iha rai, illa ne'e iha espésie naturál uitoan de'it. Tanba Timór nunka liga ho Ázia ka Austrália liuhusi rai, mamíferu boot sira la bele hakur estreitu kle'an sira. Tan ne'e, lista mamíferu nasaun nian, ne'ebé bazeia ba IUCN nia Lista Mean, iha niki barak liu.
text.pt: Os mamíferos são animais que respiram ar, têm pelo e alimentam as crias com leite. Os seres humanos também são mamíferos. Em Timor-Leste há mamíferos em terra, no ar e no mar: os morcegos são os únicos mamíferos que voam, e as baleias, os golfinhos e o dugongo vivem no oceano (ver o artigo sobre esses animais). Em terra, porém, a ilha tem poucas espécies nativas. Como Timor nunca esteve ligada por terra à Ásia nem à Austrália, os grandes mamíferos não conseguiram atravessar os estreitos profundos. Por isso, a lista de mamíferos do país, baseada na Lista Vermelha da IUCN, é dominada pelos morcegos.
text.en: Mammals are animals that breathe air, have hair and feed their young with milk. Humans are mammals too. In Timor-Leste there are mammals on land, in the air and in the sea: bats are the only mammals that fly, and whales, dolphins and the dugong live in the ocean (see the article on these animals). On land, however, the island has few native species. Because Timor was never joined by land to Asia or Australia, large mammals could not cross the deep straits. That is why the country's list of mammals, based on the IUCN Red List, is dominated by bats.
text.id: Mamalia adalah hewan yang menghirup udara, berambut, dan menyusui anaknya. Manusia juga mamalia. Di Timor-Leste ada mamalia di darat, di udara, dan di laut: kelelawar adalah satu-satunya mamalia yang terbang, sedangkan paus, lumba-lumba, dan dugong hidup di samudra (lihat artikel tentang hewan-hewan itu). Namun, di darat pulau ini hanya memiliki sedikit spesies asli. Karena Timor tidak pernah tersambung dengan Asia maupun Australia melalui daratan, mamalia besar tidak dapat menyeberangi selat-selat yang dalam. Itulah sebabnya daftar mamalia negara ini, yang didasarkan pada Daftar Merah IUCN, didominasi oleh kelelawar.

heading.tet: Niki: mamíferu ne'ebé iha espésie barak liu
heading.pt: Morcegos: os mamíferos com mais espécies
heading.en: Bats: the mammals with the most species

text.tet: Niki sira to'o Timór rasik ho semo, no ohin loron sira mak grupu mamíferu ne'ebé iha espésie barak liu iha illa. Estudu klásiku ida, ne'ebé Muzeu Amerikanu Istória Naturál nian publika iha 1979, deskreve Timór nia niki sira. Iha grupu boot rua. Niki boot ne'ebé han ai-fuan (iha portugés “raposa-voadora”) haree di'ak no han ai-fuan, ai-funan no ai-funan nia been; bainhira sira semo husi ai-hun ida ba seluk, sira fahe fini no poliniza ai-funan. Iha sira-nia leet iha Pteropus vampyrus, ne'ebé barak iha Dili nia haleu tuir ema ne'ebé observa animál, no Acerodon mackloti, ne'ebé iha kategoria Vulneravel. Niki ki'ik sira kaer insetu iha kalan ho sira-nia lian nia eku, no toba iha fatuk-kuak. Niki-ferradura Timór (Rhinolophus montanus) ema hatene de'it iha Timór, no nia iha perigu.
text.pt: Os morcegos chegaram a Timor sozinhos, a voar, e hoje são o grupo de mamíferos com mais espécies na ilha. Um estudo clássico, publicado em 1979 pelo Museu Americano de História Natural, descreveu os morcegos de Timor. Há dois grandes grupos. As raposas-voadoras e outros morcegos-da-fruta são grandes, veem bem e comem fruta, flores e néctar; ao voar de árvore em árvore espalham sementes e polinizam flores. Entre eles estão a raposa-voadora-grande (Pteropus vampyrus), comum à volta de Díli segundo observadores de animais, e a raposa-voadora-de-sunda (Acerodon mackloti), classificada como Vulnerável. Os morcegos pequenos caçam insetos à noite guiando-se pelo eco dos seus gritos e dormem em grutas. O morcego-de-ferradura-de-timor (Rhinolophus montanus) só é conhecido em Timor e está Em Perigo.
text.en: Bats reached Timor on their own, by flying, and today they are the group of mammals with the most species on the island. A classic study, published in 1979 by the American Museum of Natural History, described the bats of Timor. There are two main groups. Flying foxes and other fruit bats are large, see well and eat fruit, flowers and nectar; as they fly from tree to tree they spread seeds and pollinate flowers. They include the large flying fox (Pteropus vampyrus), common around Dili according to wildlife watchers, and the Sunda flying fox (Acerodon mackloti), listed as Vulnerable. Small bats hunt insects at night, finding their way by the echoes of their calls, and sleep in caves. The Timorese horseshoe bat (Rhinolophus montanus) is known only from Timor and is Endangered.
text.id: Kelelawar sampai di Timor sendiri dengan terbang, dan kini menjadi kelompok mamalia dengan spesies terbanyak di pulau ini. Sebuah penelitian klasik yang diterbitkan pada 1979 oleh Museum Sejarah Alam Amerika (American Museum of Natural History) menggambarkan kelelawar Timor. Ada dua kelompok besar. Kalong dan kelelawar buah lainnya bertubuh besar, penglihatannya baik, dan memakan buah, bunga, serta nektar; saat terbang dari pohon ke pohon, mereka menyebarkan biji dan menyerbuki bunga. Di antaranya kalong besar (Pteropus vampyrus), yang menurut para pengamat satwa banyak terdapat di sekitar Dili, dan kalong sunda (Acerodon mackloti), yang berstatus Rentan. Kelelawar kecil berburu serangga pada malam hari dengan berpedoman pada gema suaranya, dan tidur di gua. Kelelawar ladam timor (Rhinolophus montanus) hanya dikenal di Timor dan berstatus Terancam.

heading.tet: Laho sira: uluk no ohin loron
heading.pt: Ratos: do passado e de hoje

text.tet: Laho sira to'o Timór kleur ona, karik namlele iha ai-horis nia leten ne'ebé tasi lori, no iha illa ne'e sira sai espésie rasik. Ruin ne'ebé ema hetan iha fatuk-kuak sira iha Timór-Leste hatudu katak uluk laho boot sira moris iha ne'e, boot liu laho ohin loron nian. Sira lakon ona, no sientista sira sei estuda bainhira no tanba saida (haree artigu kona-ba animál tempu jelu nian). Karik sei iha laho naturál balu iha ai-laran foho nian, maibé ita hatene uitoan de'it kona-ba sira. Laho ne'ebé tama uma, armazén no to'os barak liu mak espésie ne'ebé mai hamutuk ho ema. Sira han hare, batar no ai-han seluk, no bele hada'et moras, tan ne'e di'ak liu rai hahán iha fatin ne'ebé taka metin no hamoos uma beibeik.
text.pt: Os ratos chegaram a Timor há muito tempo, provavelmente em jangadas de plantas levadas pelo mar, e na ilha transformaram-se em espécies próprias. Os ossos encontrados em grutas de Timor-Leste mostram que viveram aqui ratos gigantes, muito maiores do que os de hoje. Desapareceram, e os cientistas ainda estudam quando e porquê (ver o artigo sobre os animais da Idade do Gelo). Talvez ainda vivam ratos nativos nas florestas de montanha, mas sabe-se muito pouco sobre eles. Os ratos que entram nas casas, nos armazéns e nos campos são sobretudo espécies que vieram com as pessoas. Comem arroz, milho e outras colheitas e podem transmitir doenças, por isso convém guardar a comida em recipientes bem fechados e manter as casas limpas.
text.en: Rats reached Timor long ago, probably on rafts of plants carried by the sea, and on the island they turned into species of their own. Bones found in caves in Timor-Leste show that giant rats, much bigger than today's, once lived here. They disappeared, and scientists are still studying when and why (see the article on the animals of the Ice Age). Native rats may still live in the mountain forests, but very little is known about them. The rats that get into houses, storerooms and fields are mostly species that came with people. They eat rice, maize and other crops and can spread diseases, so it is wise to keep food in tightly closed containers and to keep houses clean.
text.id: Tikus sampai di Timor sejak lama, mungkin di atas rakit tumbuhan yang terbawa laut, dan di pulau ini mereka berubah menjadi spesies tersendiri. Tulang-tulang yang ditemukan di gua-gua di Timor-Leste menunjukkan bahwa dulu tikus raksasa, yang jauh lebih besar daripada tikus sekarang, pernah hidup di sini. Tikus raksasa itu sudah lenyap, dan para ilmuwan masih meneliti kapan dan mengapa (lihat artikel tentang hewan Zaman Es). Mungkin masih ada tikus asli yang hidup di hutan pegunungan, tetapi sangat sedikit yang diketahui tentang mereka. Tikus yang masuk ke rumah, gudang, dan ladang sebagian besar adalah spesies yang datang bersama manusia. Tikus memakan padi, jagung, dan hasil panen lain serta dapat menularkan penyakit, jadi sebaiknya makanan disimpan dalam wadah yang tertutup rapat dan rumah dijaga tetap bersih.

text.tet: Mamíferu fuik seluk iha Timór mai husi animál ne'ebé ema lori mai. Rusa (Rusa timorensis, ema mós bolu bibi-rusa) hetan nia naran sientífiku husi animál ida husi Timór, maibé nia mai husi Java no Bali; rusa mane iha dikur ne'ebé monu no tubu fali kada tinan. Lekirauk ikun-naruk (Macaca fascicularis) moris iha grupu, han ai-fuan, ai-tahan, insetu no kadiuk, no dala ruma tama to'os. Kuskus Timór nian mak Phalanger orientalis: animál marsupiál ida ne'ebé la'o neineik, moris iha ai leten, sai iha kalan no rai nia oan iha bolsa. Laku (Paradoxurus hermaphroditus) sai mós iha kalan atu han ai-fuan no animál ki'ik. Iha Lista Mean mundiál, rusa iha kategoria Vulneravel no lekirauk iha kategoria Iha Perigu.
text.pt: Os outros mamíferos selvagens de Timor descendem de animais trazidos por pessoas. O veado-de-timor (Rusa timorensis, bibi-rusa em tétum) recebeu o nome científico a partir de um exemplar de Timor, mas é originário de Java e Bali; os machos têm hastes que caem e voltam a crescer todos os anos. O macaco-de-cauda-longa (Macaca fascicularis, lekirauk) vive em grupos, come fruta, folhas, insetos e caranguejos e entra por vezes nas hortas. O cusco de Timor é o cusco-comum-do-norte (Phalanger orientalis): um marsupial lento e noturno que vive nas árvores e guarda a cria numa bolsa. A civeta-das-palmeiras (Paradoxurus hermaphroditus, laku) também sai à noite para comer fruta e pequenos animais. Na Lista Vermelha mundial, o veado é Vulnerável e o macaco está Em Perigo.
text.en: Timor's other wild mammals descend from animals brought by people. The Timor deer (Rusa timorensis, bibi-rusa in Tetun) was given its scientific name from a specimen from Timor, but it comes originally from Java and Bali; the males have antlers that fall off and grow back every year. The long-tailed macaque (Macaca fascicularis, lekirauk) lives in groups, eats fruit, leaves, insects and crabs, and sometimes gets into vegetable gardens. Timor's cuscus is the northern common cuscus (Phalanger orientalis): a slow, nocturnal marsupial that lives in trees and keeps its young in a pouch. The Asian palm civet (Paradoxurus hermaphroditus, laku) also comes out at night to eat fruit and small animals. On the global Red List, the deer is Vulnerable and the macaque is Endangered.
text.id: Mamalia liar lainnya di Timor merupakan keturunan hewan yang dibawa manusia. Rusa timor (Rusa timorensis, bibi-rusa dalam bahasa Tetun) mendapat nama ilmiahnya dari spesimen asal Timor, tetapi aslinya berasal dari Jawa dan Bali; rusa jantan memiliki tanduk yang lepas dan tumbuh kembali setiap tahun. Monyet ekor panjang (Macaca fascicularis, lekirauk) hidup berkelompok, memakan buah, daun, serangga, dan kepiting, dan kadang-kadang masuk ke kebun. Kuskus di Timor adalah kuskus abu-abu (Phalanger orientalis): hewan berkantung yang lamban, aktif pada malam hari, hidup di pohon, dan menyimpan anaknya di dalam kantung. Musang luwak (Paradoxurus hermaphroditus, laku) juga keluar pada malam hari untuk memakan buah dan hewan kecil. Dalam Daftar Merah dunia, rusa berstatus Rentan dan monyet berstatus Terancam.

text.tet: Durante sékulu barak, timoroan kasa rusa no animál seluk atu han, no ema barak sei gosta na'an-rusa. Kasa barak liu, ahi no ko'a ai-laran halo animál sira-ne'e sai raru, tan ne'e kasa tenke tuir lei no tara bandu nia regra. Fatuk-kuak ne'ebé niki toba ba presiza kuidadu espesiál: barullu, ahi no lixu bele duni sai niki hotu husi fatin ne'e, no niki ajuda to'os-na'in sira tanba sira han insetu barak. Ba ita-nia saúde, keta kaer niki, lekirauk ka animál fuik seluk ne'ebé kanek, tanba sira bele tata no hada'et moras. Keta fó hahán ba lekirauk, tanba sira toman ema no bele tata. Se ó haree animál raru ida, ó bele rejista ho foto, data no fatin.
text.pt: Durante séculos, os timorenses caçaram veados e outros animais para comer, e a carne de veado continua a ser apreciada. A caça excessiva, os incêndios e o corte das florestas tornam estes animais mais raros, por isso a caça deve respeitar a lei e as regras do tara bandu. As grutas onde dormem morcegos merecem cuidado especial: barulho, fogo e lixo podem expulsar colónias inteiras, e os morcegos ajudam os agricultores porque comem muitos insetos. Para a nossa saúde, nunca devemos pegar em morcegos, macacos ou outros animais selvagens feridos, porque podem morder e transmitir doenças. Também não se deve dar comida aos macacos, que se habituam às pessoas e podem morder. Quem vir um animal raro pode registá-lo com fotografia, data e lugar.
text.en: For centuries the Timorese have hunted deer and other animals for food, and venison is still popular. Too much hunting, fires and the cutting of forests are making these animals rarer, so hunting must respect the law and the rules of tara bandu. Caves where bats sleep need special care: noise, fire and rubbish can drive out whole colonies, and bats help farmers because they eat a lot of insects. For our own health, we should never handle bats, monkeys or other wild animals that are injured, because they can bite and spread diseases. Nor should anyone feed monkeys, which get used to people and may bite. Anyone who sees a rare animal can record it with a photo, the date and the place.
text.id: Selama berabad-abad orang Timor berburu rusa dan hewan lain untuk dimakan, dan daging rusa masih digemari. Perburuan berlebihan, kebakaran, dan penebangan hutan membuat hewan-hewan ini makin langka, karena itu perburuan harus mematuhi hukum dan aturan tara bandu. Gua tempat kelelawar tidur perlu dijaga secara khusus: kebisingan, api, dan sampah dapat mengusir seluruh koloni, dan kelelawar membantu petani karena memakan banyak serangga. Demi kesehatan kita, jangan pernah memegang kelelawar, monyet, atau satwa liar lain yang terluka, karena mereka bisa menggigit dan menularkan penyakit. Jangan pula memberi makan monyet, karena monyet menjadi terbiasa dengan manusia dan bisa menggigit. Siapa pun yang melihat hewan langka dapat mencatatnya dengan foto, tanggal, dan tempat.

why.id: Tanduk rusa lepas dan tumbuh kembali setiap tahun, berbeda dengan tanduk kerbau yang tetap ada seumur hidup.

why.pt: Na sua área de origem, na Ásia, muitos macacos foram capturados para laboratórios e as suas florestas foram destruídas, por isso a IUCN classificou-o como Em Perigo.
why.en: In its home range in Asia, many macaques were caught for laboratories and their forests were destroyed, so the IUCN listed it as Endangered.
why.id: Di wilayah asalnya di Asia, banyak monyet ditangkap untuk laboratorium dan hutannya dirusak, sehingga IUCN menggolongkannya sebagai Terancam.

title.tet: Réptil no anfíbiu sira
title.pt: Répteis e anfíbios
title.en: Reptiles and amphibians
title.id: Reptil dan amfibi

summary.tet: La'ós lafaek de'it: Timór-Leste iha réptil no anfíbiu espésie sanulu barak, hanesan teki, lagartu, varanu, samea, lenuk no manduku. Estudu sira ne'ebé sai iha 2011 no 2015 hasa'e lista espésie ne'ebé ema hatene husi 22 ba liu 60, no barak seidauk iha naran sientífiku. Samea balu de'it mak iha venenu, maibé ema hotu tenke hatene oinsá atu hadook an no halo saida bainhira samea tata.
summary.pt: Além do crocodilo, Timor-Leste tem dezenas de répteis e anfíbios: osgas, lagartixas, varanos, cobras, tartarugas, rãs e sapos. Estudos publicados em 2011 e 2015 fizeram crescer a lista conhecida de 22 para mais de 60 espécies, muitas ainda sem nome científico. Só algumas cobras são venenosas, mas todos devem saber evitar e tratar uma mordedura.
summary.en: Besides the crocodile, Timor-Leste has dozens of reptiles and amphibians: geckos, skinks, monitor lizards, snakes, turtles, frogs and toads. Studies published in 2011 and 2015 raised the known list from 22 to more than 60 species, many of them still without a scientific name. Only a few snakes are venomous, but everyone should know how to avoid and treat a bite.
summary.id: Selain buaya, Timor-Leste memiliki puluhan jenis reptil dan amfibi: cicak, kadal, biawak, ular, kura-kura, katak, dan kodok. Penelitian yang diterbitkan pada 2011 dan 2015 menambah daftar yang diketahui dari 22 menjadi lebih dari 60 spesies, banyak di antaranya belum memiliki nama ilmiah. Hanya sebagian kecil ular yang berbisa, tetapi semua orang perlu tahu cara menghindari dan menangani gigitan.

heading.pt: Uma lista que não para de crescer

text.tet: To'o foin daudauk, ema hatene uitoan de'it kona-ba réptil no anfíbiu iha Timór-Leste: lista tuan sira iha espésie 22 de'it. Hafoin independénsia, ekipa sira ne'ebé erpetólogu (espesialista réptil no anfíbiu nian) Hinrich Kaiser lidera, la'o iha nasaun laran atu buka animál sira-ne'e, loron no kalan. Relatóriu dahuluk, ne'ebé sai iha 2011 iha revista sientífika ZooKeys, estuda ezemplár 263: anfíbiu 100 no réptil 163. Revizaun ida ne'ebé sai iha 2015, ho estudu iha terenu husi 2011 to'o 2013, hasa'e lista ba espésie liu 60, no liu 20 husi sira seidauk iha naran sientífiku: karik sira espésie foun ba siénsia. Estudu sira la'o iha distritu tuan hotu, maibé la to'o Oe-Kusi Ambenu, tan ne'e sei iha buat barak atu deskobre.
text.pt: Até há pouco tempo, os répteis e anfíbios de Timor-Leste eram mal conhecidos: as listas antigas tinham apenas 22 espécies. Depois da independência, equipas lideradas pelo herpetólogo Hinrich Kaiser percorreram o país à procura destes animais, de dia e de noite. O primeiro relatório, publicado em 2011 na revista científica ZooKeys, estudou 263 exemplares: 100 anfíbios e 163 répteis. Uma revisão publicada em 2015, com trabalho de campo feito entre 2011 e 2013, elevou a lista para mais de 60 espécies, e mais de 20 delas ainda não tinham nome científico: podem ser espécies novas para a ciência. Os estudos passaram por todos os antigos distritos, exceto Oé-Cusse, por isso ainda há muito para descobrir.
text.en: Until recently, the reptiles and amphibians of Timor-Leste were poorly known: the old lists had only 22 species. After independence, teams led by the herpetologist Hinrich Kaiser travelled around the country looking for these animals, by day and by night. The first report, published in 2011 in the scientific journal ZooKeys, studied 263 specimens: 100 amphibians and 163 reptiles. A review published in 2015, based on fieldwork carried out between 2011 and 2013, raised the list to more than 60 species, and more than 20 of them still had no scientific name: they may be species new to science. The studies covered all the former districts except Oé-Cusse Ambeno, so there is still a lot to discover.
text.id: Sampai belum lama ini, reptil dan amfibi Timor-Leste kurang dikenal: daftar lama hanya memuat 22 spesies. Setelah kemerdekaan, tim yang dipimpin ahli herpetologi Hinrich Kaiser menjelajahi negeri ini untuk mencari hewan-hewan tersebut, siang dan malam. Laporan pertama, yang diterbitkan pada 2011 dalam jurnal ilmiah ZooKeys, meneliti 263 spesimen: 100 amfibi dan 163 reptil. Sebuah tinjauan yang diterbitkan pada 2015, dengan kerja lapangan antara 2011 dan 2013, menambah daftar itu menjadi lebih dari 60 spesies, dan lebih dari 20 di antaranya belum memiliki nama ilmiah: mungkin spesies baru bagi ilmu pengetahuan. Penelitian itu menjangkau semua bekas distrik kecuali Oé-Cusse Ambeno, jadi masih banyak yang belum ditemukan.

text.tet: Teki mak réptil ne'ebé ita haree barak liu, tanba sira moris iha uma nia didin. Iha kalan sira hein besik lámpada atu kaer insetu ne'ebé naroman dada mai. Teki boot liu mak teki tokay, no ninia naran “teki” hanesan ninia lian makaas. Lagartu ki'ik ne'ebé mamar no nabilan (eskinku) halai iha ai-tahan maran no fatuk sira-nia leet iha loro-matan. Varanu mak lagartu boot liu, ho nanál fahe rua hanesan samea nian: varanu Timór ki'ik (Varanus timorensis) sa'e ai-hun no kaer insetu, manu-tolun no animál ki'ik. Iha Atauru, estudu ida iha 2013 temi varanu ne'ebé karik espésie ida seidauk iha naran. Lagartu hotu-hotu ne'e ajuda kontrola insetu, no la halo aat ema se ita husik sira hakmatek.
text.pt: As osgas são os répteis que mais vemos, porque vivem nas paredes das casas. À noite esperam perto das lâmpadas para apanhar os insetos atraídos pela luz. A maior é a osga-tokay, chamada teki em tétum, um nome que lembra o seu grito forte. As lagartixas lisas e brilhantes (escincos) correm entre as folhas secas e as pedras ao sol. Os varanos são lagartos maiores, com a língua bifurcada como a das cobras: o pequeno varano-de-timor (Varanus timorensis) sobe às árvores e caça insetos, ovos e pequenos animais. Em Ataúro, um estudo de 2013 referiu varanos que podem pertencer a uma espécie ainda por descrever. Todos estes lagartos ajudam a controlar os insetos e são inofensivos se os deixarmos em paz.
text.en: Geckos are the reptiles we see most often, because they live on the walls of houses. At night they wait near light bulbs to catch the insects drawn to the light. The largest is the tokay gecko, called teki in Tetun, a name that sounds like its loud call. Smooth, shiny skinks scurry among dry leaves and over stones in the sun. Monitor lizards are bigger lizards with a forked tongue like a snake's: the small Timor monitor (Varanus timorensis) climbs trees and hunts insects, eggs and small animals. On Ataúro, a 2013 study mentioned monitor lizards that may belong to a species not yet described. All these lizards help to control insects and are harmless if we leave them alone.
text.id: Cicak adalah reptil yang paling sering kita lihat, karena hidup di dinding rumah. Pada malam hari cicak menunggu di dekat lampu untuk menangkap serangga yang tertarik oleh cahaya. Yang terbesar adalah tokek, yang dalam bahasa Tetun disebut teki, nama yang mirip dengan suaranya yang keras. Kadal yang licin dan mengilap berlarian di antara daun kering dan bebatuan di bawah sinar matahari. Biawak adalah kadal yang lebih besar, dengan lidah bercabang seperti lidah ular: biawak timor (Varanus timorensis) yang kecil memanjat pohon dan berburu serangga, telur, dan hewan kecil. Di Ataúro, sebuah penelitian tahun 2013 menyebut biawak yang mungkin termasuk spesies yang belum dideskripsikan. Semua kadal ini membantu mengendalikan serangga dan tidak berbahaya jika kita membiarkannya.

text.tet: Timór-Leste iha samea oioin, no barak liu la halo aat ema no ajuda ita, tanba sira han laho. Samea ne'ebé ema bolu “pitaun Timór” (Malayopython timoriensis) iha naran ne'ebé lohi ema: nia moris iha Flores no illa besik, no karik la iha iha Timór. Pitaun ne'ebé ema hetan iha Timór mak Liasis mackloti, samea ida ne'ebé kaer metin nia hahán ho nia isin to'o mate no moris besik bee. Kona-ba lenuk, lenuk tasi nian espésie oioin mai iha kosta (haree artigu kona-ba espésie iha perigu). Iha Lagoa Ira Lalaro nia área, iha Lautein, moris lenuk ida ne'ebé raru tebes, ne'ebé hela iha lagoa no mota no iha kakorok naruk hanesan samea: iha 2007, sientista sira deskreve nia hanesan subespésie rasik, Chelodina mccordi timorensis. Espésie ne'e iha perigu boot tebes.
text.pt: Timor-Leste tem várias cobras, e a maioria é inofensiva e útil, porque come ratos. A chamada «pitão-de-timor» (Malayopython timoriensis) tem um nome enganador: vive em Flores e em ilhas vizinhas, e provavelmente não existe em Timor. A pitão que se encontra em Timor é a pitão-de-macklot (Liasis mackloti), uma cobra que aperta as presas até morrerem e vive perto da água. Entre as tartarugas, várias espécies marinhas visitam a costa (ver o artigo sobre as espécies ameaçadas). Na zona do lago Ira Lalaro, em Lautém, vive uma tartaruga de água doce muito rara, de pescoço comprido como uma cobra: em 2007, os cientistas descreveram-na como uma subespécie própria, Chelodina mccordi timorensis. A espécie está Criticamente em Perigo.
text.en: Timor-Leste has several kinds of snake, and most are harmless and useful, because they eat rats. The so-called “Timor python” (Malayopython timoriensis) has a misleading name: it lives on Flores and nearby islands, and probably does not occur on Timor. The python found on Timor is Macklot's python (Liasis mackloti), a snake that squeezes its prey to death and lives near water. Among the turtles, several sea species visit the coast (see the article on endangered species). In the Lake Ira Lalaro area, in Lautém, lives a very rare freshwater turtle with a long neck like a snake: in 2007 scientists described it as a subspecies of its own, Chelodina mccordi timorensis. The species is Critically Endangered.
text.id: Timor-Leste memiliki beberapa jenis ular, dan sebagian besar tidak berbahaya dan berguna karena memakan tikus. Ular yang disebut “sanca timor” (Malayopython timoriensis) memiliki nama yang menyesatkan: ular ini hidup di Flores dan pulau-pulau sekitarnya, dan kemungkinan tidak ada di Timor. Sanca yang ditemukan di Timor adalah sanca air (Liasis mackloti), ular yang melilit mangsanya sampai mati dan hidup di dekat air. Di antara kura-kura, beberapa jenis penyu mengunjungi pantai (lihat artikel tentang spesies terancam punah). Di kawasan Danau Ira Lalaro, di Lautém, hidup sejenis kura-kura air tawar yang sangat langka, dengan leher panjang seperti ular: pada 2007 para ilmuwan mendeskripsikannya sebagai subspesies tersendiri, Chelodina mccordi timorensis. Spesies ini berstatus Kritis.

text.tet: Anfíbiu sira iha kulit bokon no presiza bee mota ka lagoa nian atu tau tolun, no husi tolun sira-ne'e mosu oan ki'ik ho ikun (girinu). Iha estudu sira iha Timór-Leste, anfíbiu ne'ebé barak liu mak sapu, manduku natar nian no manduku ne'ebé moris iha ai leten. Iha tempu udan, manduku mane sira hakilar hamutuk iha bee-lihun no natar atu dada feto sira. Anfíbiu sira han susuk no insetu seluk barak, no sira mós sai hahán ba samea, manu no ikan. Tanba sira dada iis balu liuhusi kulit, sira terus makaas tanba poluisaun, pestisida no seka: bainhira manduku lakon husi fatin ida, ne'e sinál ida katak bee la di'ak. Manduku balu ne'ebé ema hetan iha Timór-Leste karik sei hein naran sientífiku.
text.pt: Os anfíbios têm a pele húmida e precisam de água doce para pôr os ovos, de onde nascem girinos. Nos estudos feitos em Timor-Leste, os mais comuns foram os sapos, as rãs dos arrozais e as rãs-arborícolas. Na estação das chuvas, os machos coaxam em coro nas poças e nos campos de arroz para atrair as fêmeas. Os anfíbios comem muitos mosquitos e outros insetos e são comida para cobras, aves e peixes. Como respiram em parte pela pele, sofrem muito com a poluição, os pesticidas e a seca: quando as rãs desaparecem de um lugar, é sinal de que a água não está bem. Algumas rãs encontradas em Timor-Leste talvez ainda esperem por um nome científico.
text.en: Amphibians have moist skin and need fresh water to lay their eggs, which hatch into tadpoles. In the studies carried out in Timor-Leste, the most common were toads, rice-field frogs and tree frogs. In the rainy season, the males croak in chorus in puddles and rice fields to attract females. Amphibians eat many mosquitoes and other insects and are food for snakes, birds and fish. Because they breathe partly through their skin, they suffer badly from pollution, pesticides and drought: when frogs disappear from a place, it is a sign that the water is not healthy. Some frogs found in Timor-Leste may still be waiting for a scientific name.
text.id: Amfibi memiliki kulit yang lembap dan memerlukan air tawar untuk bertelur; dari telur itu menetas berudu. Dalam penelitian di Timor-Leste, yang paling umum adalah kodok, katak sawah, dan katak pohon. Pada musim hujan, katak jantan berbunyi bersahut-sahutan di genangan air dan sawah untuk menarik betina. Amfibi memakan banyak nyamuk dan serangga lain dan menjadi makanan bagi ular, burung, dan ikan. Karena sebagian bernapas melalui kulit, amfibi sangat menderita akibat pencemaran, pestisida, dan kekeringan: jika katak menghilang dari suatu tempat, itu tanda bahwa airnya tidak baik. Beberapa katak yang ditemukan di Timor-Leste mungkin masih menunggu nama ilmiah.

heading.tet: Samea ho venenu: oinsá atu seguru
heading.en: Venomous snakes: how to stay safe

text.tet: Samea ho venenu ne'ebé barak liu iha rai mak Trimeresurus insularis, samea matak ida ho ibun nia sorin mutin ne'ebé moris iha ai-hun no ai-tahan sira-nia leet; iha estudu sira, nia mak liu parte ida husi haat husi samea hotu ne'ebé ema hetan. Nia kaer hahán iha kalan no hela hakmatek, tan ne'e ita la haree nia fasil. Iha tasi moris samea tasi nian ho venenu makaas, maibé sira tata ema raru. Atu evita samea tata: hatais sapatu taka bainhira la'o iha ai-laran, lori lanterna iha kalan, no haree uluk molok tau liman iha ai-tahan ka ai-maran nia leet. Keta koko kaer ka oho samea. Se samea tata ema ida, halo nia hakmatek no la book, hasai kadeli no pulseira, halo ain ka liman ne'e la book no lori lalais ba sentru saúde. Keta ko'a kanek, keta suu venenu no keta kesi metin ho tali.
text.pt: A cobra venenosa mais comum em terra é a víbora-de-lábios-brancos (Trimeresurus insularis), uma víbora verde que vive nas árvores e nos arbustos; nos estudos, foi mais de um quarto das cobras encontradas. Caça à noite e fica imóvel, por isso é fácil não a ver. No mar vivem cobras-marinhas muito venenosas, que raramente mordem. Para evitar mordeduras, use calçado fechado no mato, leve lanterna à noite e olhe antes de pôr as mãos em arbustos ou montes de lenha. Nunca tente apanhar ou matar uma cobra. Se alguém for mordido, mantenha a pessoa calma e quieta, tire anéis e pulseiras, imobilize o membro e leve-a depressa ao centro de saúde. Não corte a ferida, não chupe o veneno e não aperte o membro com cordas.
text.en: The most common venomous snake on land is the white-lipped pit viper (Trimeresurus insularis), a green viper that lives in trees and bushes; in the studies it made up more than a quarter of the snakes found. It hunts at night and keeps very still, so it is easy to miss. In the sea live highly venomous sea snakes, which rarely bite. To avoid bites, wear closed shoes in the bush, carry a torch at night and look before putting your hands into bushes or piles of firewood. Never try to catch or kill a snake. If someone is bitten, keep the person calm and still, remove rings and bracelets, immobilise the limb and take them quickly to the health centre. Do not cut the wound, do not suck out the venom and do not tie cords tightly around the limb.
text.id: Ular berbisa yang paling umum di darat adalah viper bibir putih (Trimeresurus insularis), ular viper hijau yang hidup di pohon dan semak; dalam penelitian itu, jenis ini mencakup lebih dari seperempat ular yang ditemukan. Ular ini berburu pada malam hari dan diam tak bergerak, jadi mudah luput dari pandangan. Di laut hidup ular laut yang sangat berbisa, tetapi jarang menggigit. Untuk menghindari gigitan, pakailah sepatu tertutup di semak belukar, bawalah senter pada malam hari, dan lihatlah dulu sebelum memasukkan tangan ke semak atau tumpukan kayu bakar. Jangan pernah mencoba menangkap atau membunuh ular. Jika seseorang digigit, buatlah orang itu tetap tenang dan diam, lepaskan cincin dan gelangnya, jaga agar anggota tubuh yang digigit tidak bergerak, lalu segera bawa ke pusat kesehatan. Jangan menyayat luka, jangan mengisap bisa, dan jangan mengikat anggota tubuh itu kuat-kuat dengan tali.

q.id: Mengapa cicak menunggu di dekat lampu pada malam hari?

options.tet: Atu kaer insetu ne'ebé naroman dada mai
options.pt: Para apanhar os insetos atraídos pela luz
options.en: To catch the insects drawn to the light
options.id: Untuk menangkap serangga yang tertarik oleh cahaya

options.en: To lay eggs on the bulbs

why.tet: Naroman dada insetu barak, no teki kaer sira; ida-ne'e ajuda hamenus susuk no lalar iha uma.
why.pt: A luz atrai muitos insetos e as osgas apanham-nos, o que ajuda a reduzir mosquitos e moscas em casa.
why.en: Light attracts many insects and the geckos catch them, which helps to reduce mosquitoes and flies in the house.
why.id: Cahaya menarik banyak serangga dan cicak menangkapnya, sehingga membantu mengurangi nyamuk dan lalat di rumah.

q.tet: Se samea tata ema ida, saida mak di'ak liu atu halo?
q.pt: Se uma cobra morder alguém, o que se deve fazer?
q.en: If a snake bites someone, what should you do?
q.id: Jika ular menggigit seseorang, apa yang harus dilakukan?

options.pt: Cortar a ferida e chupar o veneno
options.en: Cut the wound and suck out the venom

options.tet: Kesi metin liman ka ain ho tali
options.pt: Apertar muito o membro com uma corda
options.en: Tie a cord very tightly around the limb
options.id: Mengikat anggota tubuh itu kuat-kuat dengan tali

options.tet: Halo nia hakmatek, la book liman ka ain, no lori lalais ba sentru saúde
options.pt: Manter a pessoa calma e quieta, imobilizar o membro e ir depressa ao centro de saúde
options.en: Keep the person calm and still, immobilise the limb and go quickly to the health centre
options.id: Membuat orang itu tetap tenang dan diam, menjaga agar anggota tubuhnya tidak bergerak, dan segera pergi ke pusat kesehatan

options.en: Wait at home for a few days

why.tet: Hakmatek no la book halo venenu la'o neineik liu iha isin; ko'a, suu ka kesi metin halo kanek aat liu.
why.pt: A calma e a imobilidade atrasam a passagem do veneno pelo corpo; cortar, chupar ou apertar com cordas só piora a situação.
why.en: Staying calm and still slows the spread of the venom through the body; cutting, sucking or tying cords only makes things worse.
why.id: Tetap tenang dan tidak bergerak memperlambat penyebaran bisa di dalam tubuh; menyayat, mengisap, atau mengikat dengan tali hanya memperburuk keadaan.

q.tet: Chelodina mccordi, ne'ebé moris iha Lagoa Ira Lalaro nia área, mak animál saida?
q.pt: Que animal é a Chelodina mccordi, que vive na zona do lago Ira Lalaro?

q.id: Hewan apakah Chelodina mccordi, yang hidup di kawasan Danau Ira Lalaro?

why.en: It is a turtle with a long neck like a snake. In 2007 scientists described the Timor-Leste population as a subspecies of its own.
why.id: Hewan ini adalah kura-kura berleher panjang seperti ular. Pada 2007 para ilmuwan mendeskripsikan populasi Timor-Leste sebagai subspesies tersendiri.

q.id: Di mana sebenarnya “sanca timor” (Malayopython timoriensis) hidup?

options.tet: Iha Flores no illa besik; karik la iha iha Timór

why.id: Namanya menyesatkan: para ahli mengatakan sanca ini hidup di Flores dan pulau-pulau sekitarnya, bukan di Timor.

title.tet: Baleia, golfiñu no dugongu
title.pt: Baleias, golfinhos e dugongos
title.en: Whales, dolphins and dugongs
title.id: Paus, lumba-lumba, dan dugong

summary.tet: Tasi kle'an besik Dili no Atauru halo ema bele haree baleia no golfiñu iha kilómetru balu de'it husi kosta. Ema rejista ona espésie liu 20, no baleia azúl ki'ik sira liu liuliu entre Outubru no Dezembru. Dugongu, mamíferu tasi nian ne'ebé han du'ut-tasi, raru no presiza protesaun.
summary.pt: As águas profundas perto de Díli e de Ataúro permitem ver baleias e golfinhos a poucos quilómetros da costa. Já foram registadas mais de 20 espécies, e as baleias-azuis-pigmeias passam sobretudo entre outubro e dezembro. O dugongo, um mamífero marinho que come ervas marinhas, é raro e precisa de proteção.
summary.en: The deep waters near Dili and Ataúro make it possible to see whales and dolphins just a few kilometres from the coast. More than 20 species have been recorded, and pygmy blue whales pass by mainly between October and December. The dugong, a sea mammal that eats seagrass, is rare and needs protection.
summary.id: Perairan dalam di dekat Dili dan Ataúro memungkinkan orang melihat paus dan lumba-lumba hanya beberapa kilometer dari pantai. Lebih dari 20 spesies telah tercatat, dan paus biru kerdil melintas terutama antara Oktober dan Desember. Dugong, mamalia laut pemakan lamun, langka dan perlu dilindungi.

heading.en: Mammals that live in the sea

text.tet: Baleia, golfiñu no dugongu hanesan ikan, maibé sira mamíferu: sira dada iis, hahoris oan moris no fó susu ba sira. Baleia no golfiñu (setáseu) sa'e ba tasi leten atu dada iis liuhusi kuak ida iha ulun leten, no anin no bee ne'ebé sira huu sai, ema bele haree husi dook. Iha grupu rua. Baleia ho barba, hanesan baleia azúl, la iha nehan: sira filtra tasi-been barak tebes atu kaer animál ki'ik ho barba sira iha sira-nia ibun. Baleia ho nehan, hanesan kaxalote, baleia pilotu no golfiñu, kaer ikan no lula, no buka dalan ho sira-nia lian nia eku. Dugongu mak grupu seluk (sirénia) no han ai-horis.
text.pt: Baleias, golfinhos e dugongos parecem peixes, mas são mamíferos: respiram ar, dão à luz crias vivas e alimentam-nas com leite. As baleias e os golfinhos (cetáceos) sobem à superfície para respirar por um orifício no alto da cabeça, e o jato de ar e água que expulsam vê-se de longe. Há dois grupos. As baleias de barbas, como a baleia-azul, não têm dentes: filtram enormes quantidades de água para apanhar pequenos animais com as placas de barbas que têm na boca. As baleias de dentes, como o cachalote, as baleias-piloto e os golfinhos, caçam peixes e lulas e orientam-se pelo eco dos sons que emitem. O dugongo pertence a outro grupo, os sirénios, e alimenta-se de plantas.
text.en: Whales, dolphins and dugongs look like fish, but they are mammals: they breathe air, give birth to live young and feed them with milk. Whales and dolphins (cetaceans) come up to the surface to breathe through a blowhole on top of the head, and the spout of air and water they blow out can be seen from far away. There are two groups. Baleen whales, such as the blue whale, have no teeth: they filter huge amounts of water to catch small animals with the baleen plates in their mouths. Toothed whales, such as the sperm whale, pilot whales and dolphins, hunt fish and squid and find their way by the echoes of the sounds they make. The dugong belongs to another group, the sirenians, and feeds on plants.
text.id: Paus, lumba-lumba, dan dugong tampak seperti ikan, tetapi mereka adalah mamalia: menghirup udara, melahirkan anak, dan menyusuinya. Paus dan lumba-lumba (setasea) naik ke permukaan untuk bernapas melalui lubang di bagian atas kepala, dan semburan udara dan air yang mereka keluarkan terlihat dari jauh. Ada dua kelompok. Paus balin, seperti paus biru, tidak bergigi: mereka menyaring air dalam jumlah sangat besar untuk menangkap hewan kecil dengan lempeng balin di mulutnya. Paus bergigi, seperti paus sperma, paus pilot, dan lumba-lumba, berburu ikan dan cumi-cumi serta mencari arah dengan gema suara yang mereka keluarkan. Dugong termasuk kelompok lain, yaitu sirenia, dan memakan tumbuhan.

heading.pt: O estreito profundo, uma estrada de baleias
heading.en: The deep strait, a highway for whales
heading.id: Selat yang dalam, jalan raya paus

text.tet: Estreitu Ombai–Wetar, entre Timór, Alor, Atauru no Wetar, kle'an liu metru 3 000 besik tebes ba kosta. Liuhusi estreitu ne'e, parte husi tasi-been ne'ebé suli husi Oseanu Pasífiku ba Oseanu Índiku liu. Ho monsaun no tasi sa'e no tun (maré), tasi-been malirin ne'ebé iha hahán barak sa'e husi tasi kle'an, no ida-ne'e dada animál ki'ik, ikan, lula no animál ne'ebé han sira. Baleia azúl ki'ik, baleia azúl nia forma ki'ik liu ne'ebé bele naruk liu metru 20, uza estreitu ne'e hanesan dalan migrasaun entre Austrália nia tasi no tasi sira iha Indonézia. Sira-nia la'o ba sul mak ema haree barak liu husi Outubru to'o Dezembru, no peskizadór sira husi Charles Darwin University liga ritmu ne'e ho monsaun, maré no tasi-been malirin ne'ebé sa'e.
text.pt: O estreito de Ombai–Wetar, entre Timor, Alor, Ataúro e Wetar, tem mais de 3000 m de profundidade muito perto da costa. Por ele passa parte da corrente que leva água do oceano Pacífico para o Índico. Com as monções e as marés, a água fria e rica em alimento sobe das profundezas, e isso atrai pequenos animais, peixes, lulas e quem os come. As baleias-azuis-pigmeias, uma forma mais pequena da baleia-azul que pode passar dos 20 metros, usam o estreito como corredor de migração entre as águas da Austrália e os mares da Indonésia. A passagem para sul é mais visível de outubro a dezembro, e investigadores da Charles Darwin University ligam o seu ritmo às monções, às marés e à subida de água fria.
text.en: The Ombai–Wetar Strait, between Timor, Alor, Ataúro and Wetar, is more than 3,000 m deep very close to the coast. Part of the current that carries water from the Pacific Ocean to the Indian Ocean flows through it. With the monsoons and the tides, cold, food-rich water rises from the depths, and this attracts small animals, fish, squid and the animals that eat them. Pygmy blue whales, a smaller form of the blue whale that can grow to more than 20 metres, use the strait as a migration corridor between Australian waters and the seas of Indonesia. Their journey south is most visible from October to December, and researchers from Charles Darwin University link its timing to the monsoons, the tides and the upwelling of cold water.
text.id: Selat Ombai–Wetar, di antara Timor, Alor, Ataúro, dan Wetar, dalamnya lebih dari 3.000 m sangat dekat dengan pantai. Melalui selat ini mengalir sebagian arus yang membawa air dari Samudra Pasifik ke Samudra Hindia. Bersama angin muson dan pasang surut, air dingin yang kaya makanan naik dari kedalaman, dan hal ini menarik hewan-hewan kecil, ikan, cumi-cumi, serta pemangsanya. Paus biru kerdil, bentuk paus biru yang lebih kecil dengan panjang yang bisa melebihi 20 meter, memakai selat ini sebagai koridor migrasi antara perairan Australia dan laut-laut Indonesia. Perjalanannya ke selatan paling mudah terlihat dari Oktober sampai Desember, dan para peneliti Charles Darwin University mengaitkan waktunya dengan muson, pasang surut, dan naiknya air dingin.

heading.tet: Golfiñu no baleia ne'ebé hela iha ne'e
heading.pt: Golfinhos e baleias de todo o ano
heading.en: Dolphins and whales all year round

text.tet: La'ós setáseu hotu mak liu de'it. Golfiñu no baleia ki'ik liu, hanesan baleia pilotu no baleia ulun-melaun, ema bele haree iha tinan tomak. Golfiñu-rotadór moris iha grupu boot no salta sai husi bee ho fila-an dala barak. Kaxalote, ho nia ulun boot no kuadradu, mergulla metru atus ba atus, dala ruma liu metru rihun ida, atu kaer lula iha nakukun. Estudu ida husi Charles Darwin University, husi 2016 to'o 2023, konfirma katak tasi sira-ne'e simu baleia no golfiñu espésie liu 20. Turizmu nasionál temi baleia azúl ki'ik, kaxalote, baleia ulun-melaun no baleia pilotu hanesan animál ne'ebé turista sira bele haree liu iha tempu boot.
text.pt: Nem todos os cetáceos estão só de passagem. Golfinhos e baleias mais pequenas, como as baleias-piloto-de-aleta-curta e as baleias-cabeça-de-melão, podem ver-se durante todo o ano. Os golfinhos-rotadores vivem em grandes grupos e saltam fora de água a rodar sobre si mesmos. Os cachalotes, com a sua cabeça enorme e quadrada, mergulham centenas de metros, por vezes mais de mil, para caçar lulas no escuro. Um estudo da Charles Darwin University, de 2016 a 2023, confirmou que estas águas recebem mais de 20 espécies de baleias e golfinhos. O turismo nacional aponta como avistamentos prováveis na época alta a baleia-azul-pigmeia, o cachalote, a baleia-cabeça-de-melão e a baleia-piloto-de-aleta-curta.
text.en: Not all cetaceans are just passing through. Dolphins and smaller whales, such as short-finned pilot whales and melon-headed whales, can be seen all year round. Spinner dolphins live in large groups and leap out of the water, spinning around. Sperm whales, with their huge, square heads, dive hundreds of metres, sometimes more than a thousand, to hunt squid in the dark. A Charles Darwin University study, from 2016 to 2023, confirmed that more than 20 species of whales and dolphins visit these waters. The national tourism authority lists the pygmy blue whale, the sperm whale, the melon-headed whale and the short-finned pilot whale as likely sightings in the high season.
text.id: Tidak semua setasea hanya melintas. Lumba-lumba dan paus yang lebih kecil, seperti paus pilot sirip pendek dan paus kepala semangka, dapat dilihat sepanjang tahun. Lumba-lumba spinner hidup dalam kelompok besar dan melompat keluar dari air sambil berputar. Paus sperma, dengan kepalanya yang sangat besar dan persegi, menyelam ratusan meter, kadang lebih dari seribu, untuk berburu cumi-cumi dalam gelap. Sebuah penelitian Charles Darwin University dari 2016 sampai 2023 memastikan bahwa lebih dari 20 spesies paus dan lumba-lumba datang ke perairan ini. Otoritas pariwisata nasional menyebut paus biru kerdil, paus sperma, paus kepala semangka, dan paus pilot sirip pendek sebagai hewan yang mungkin terlihat pada musim puncak.

heading.pt: O dugongo, pastor das ervas marinhas
heading.en: The dugong, grazer of the seagrass meadows

text.tet: Dugongu (Dugong dugon) mak mamíferu tasi nian ida ne'ebé hakmatek no bele naruk to'o maizumenus metru 3. Nia moris iha baía ne'ebé kalma no la kle'an, no loron tomak han du'ut-tasi, hanesan karau ne'ebé han du'ut iha rai; tan ne'e, iha lian barak, ema bolu nia “baka tasi nian”. Nia bele moris tinan sanulu barak, maibé feto hahoris oan ida de'it dala ida, no hein tinan balu molok hahoris fali, tan ne'e sira-nia númeru sa'e neineik tebes. Iha mundu tomak, IUCN klasifika nia hanesan Vulneravel. Iha Timór-Leste nia raru no ema seidauk estuda barak. Perigu prinsipál sira mak rede peska ne'ebé kaer nia, kasa, ró ne'ebé baku nia, no du'ut-tasi ne'ebé lakon tanba rai-tahu no poluisaun. Proteje du'ut-tasi mak proteje dugongu.
text.pt: O dugongo (Dugong dugon) é um mamífero marinho tranquilo que pode chegar a cerca de 3 metros. Vive em baías calmas e pouco fundas e passa o dia a pastar nas pradarias de ervas marinhas, como uma vaca no campo; por isso, em várias línguas, chamam-lhe «vaca-marinha». Pode viver muitas décadas, mas a fêmea só tem uma cria de cada vez, com vários anos de intervalo, e por isso as populações recuperam muito devagar. Em todo o mundo está classificado como Vulnerável. Em Timor-Leste é raro e pouco estudado. As principais ameaças são as redes de pesca onde fica preso, a caça, os choques com barcos e a perda das ervas marinhas por causa da lama e da poluição. Proteger as ervas marinhas é proteger o dugongo.
text.en: The dugong (Dugong dugon) is a gentle sea mammal that can grow to about 3 metres. It lives in calm, shallow bays and spends the day grazing on seagrass meadows, like a cow in a field; that is why in several languages it is called a “sea cow”. It can live for many decades, but the female has only one calf at a time, several years apart, so populations recover very slowly. Worldwide it is listed as Vulnerable. In Timor-Leste it is rare and little studied. The main threats are fishing nets in which it gets caught, hunting, collisions with boats and the loss of seagrass because of mud and pollution. Protecting seagrass means protecting the dugong.
text.id: Dugong (Dugong dugon) adalah mamalia laut yang tenang dan panjangnya bisa mencapai sekitar 3 meter. Dugong hidup di teluk yang tenang dan dangkal, dan sepanjang hari merumput di padang lamun, seperti sapi di padang; karena itu dalam beberapa bahasa hewan ini disebut “sapi laut”. Dugong dapat hidup puluhan tahun, tetapi betinanya hanya melahirkan satu anak setiap kali, dengan jarak beberapa tahun, sehingga populasinya pulih sangat lambat. Di seluruh dunia dugong berstatus Rentan. Di Timor-Leste dugong langka dan belum banyak diteliti. Ancaman utamanya adalah jaring ikan yang menjeratnya, perburuan, tabrakan dengan perahu, dan hilangnya lamun akibat lumpur dan pencemaran. Melindungi lamun berarti melindungi dugong.

text.tet: Haree baleia sai atividade ida ne'ebé aumenta: iha tempu boot, operadór balu sai husi Dili ho ró, no turizmu nasionál promove tempu husi Outubru to'o Dezembru. Maibé reportajen foun balu hatete katak turizmu ne'ebé la iha regra bele hamosu problema ba baleia sira-nia migrasaun, tanba la iha regra obrigatória ka lisensa, no projetu polítika ida husi 2018 para tiha. Timór-Leste mós anunsia norma nasionál ida atu haree baleia ho responsabilidade. Prátika di'ak sira simples: hakbesik neineik husi sorin, hela dook, keta tuir ka taka animál sira-nia dalan, keta hela kleur besik sira, keta fó hahán no keta soe lixu ba tasi. Nune'e baleia sira kontinua fila mai, no turizmu kontinua lori rendimentu ba família iha kosta.
text.pt: A observação de baleias está a crescer: na época alta, vários operadores saem de Díli de barco, e o turismo nacional promove a época de outubro a dezembro. Mas reportagens recentes alertaram que o turismo sem regras pode perturbar a migração das baleias, porque não havia regras obrigatórias nem licenças e um projeto de política preparado em 2018 tinha ficado parado. Timor-Leste anunciou também uma norma nacional para a observação responsável de baleias. As boas práticas são simples: aproximar-se devagar e de lado, manter uma boa distância, nunca perseguir os animais nem lhes cortar o caminho, não ficar muito tempo junto deles, não lhes dar comida e não deitar lixo ao mar. Assim as baleias continuam a voltar, e o turismo continua a dar rendimento às famílias da costa.
text.en: Whale watching is growing: in the high season several operators take boats out from Dili, and the national tourism authority promotes the October to December season. But recent reports warned that unregulated tourism could disturb the whales' migration, because there were no binding rules or licences and a draft policy prepared in 2018 had stalled. Timor-Leste has also announced a national standard for responsible whale watching. Good practice is simple: approach slowly and from the side, keep a good distance, never chase the animals or cut across their path, do not stay with them for long, do not feed them and do not throw rubbish into the sea. That way the whales keep coming back, and tourism keeps bringing income to coastal families.
text.id: Wisata pengamatan paus terus berkembang: pada musim puncak, beberapa operator berangkat dengan perahu dari Dili, dan otoritas pariwisata nasional mempromosikan musim Oktober sampai Desember. Namun, laporan-laporan terbaru memperingatkan bahwa pariwisata tanpa aturan dapat mengganggu migrasi paus, karena belum ada aturan wajib maupun izin, dan rancangan kebijakan yang disusun pada 2018 terhenti. Timor-Leste juga telah mengumumkan standar nasional untuk pengamatan paus yang bertanggung jawab. Cara yang baik itu sederhana: mendekat perlahan dari samping, menjaga jarak yang cukup, tidak pernah mengejar hewan atau memotong jalurnya, tidak berlama-lama di dekatnya, tidak memberinya makan, dan tidak membuang sampah ke laut. Dengan begitu paus akan terus kembali, dan pariwisata terus memberi penghasilan bagi keluarga pesisir.

title.tet: Insetu, borboleta no animál ki'ik seluk
title.pt: Insetos, borboletas e outros pequenos animais
title.en: Insects, butterflies and other small animals
title.id: Serangga, kupu-kupu, dan hewan kecil lainnya

summary.tet: Insetu no animál ki'ik seluk mak animál ne'ebé barak liu iha Timór-Leste. Sira poliniza ai-funan, halo ai-tahan mate sai rai, no sai hahán ba manu, teki no manduku. Illa ne'e iha borboleta ne'ebé la iha iha fatin seluk, hanesan Troides plato ne'ebé boot, no bani fuik ne'ebé fó bani-been.
summary.pt: Os insetos e outros pequenos animais são os animais mais numerosos de Timor-Leste. Polinizam as flores, transformam as folhas mortas em solo e alimentam aves, osgas e rãs. A ilha tem borboletas que não existem em mais lado nenhum, como a grande Troides plato, e abelhas selvagens que dão mel.
summary.en: Insects and other small animals are the most numerous animals in Timor-Leste. They pollinate flowers, turn dead leaves into soil and are food for birds, geckos and frogs. The island has butterflies that exist nowhere else, such as the large Troides plato, and wild bees that produce honey.
summary.id: Serangga dan hewan kecil lainnya adalah hewan yang paling banyak jumlahnya di Timor-Leste. Mereka menyerbuki bunga, mengubah daun mati menjadi tanah, dan menjadi makanan bagi burung, cicak, dan katak. Pulau ini memiliki kupu-kupu yang tidak ada di tempat lain, seperti Troides plato yang besar, dan lebah liar yang menghasilkan madu.

heading.id: Dunia yang kecil, tetapi sangat besar

text.tet: Insetu iha ain neen no isin parte tolu: ulun, hirus-matan (tóraks) no kabun. Barak iha liras. Sira mak animál grupu ne'ebé iha espésie barak liu iha mundu, no iha Timór-Leste seidauk iha ema ida mak hatene espésie hira mak iha. Sira-nia knaar importante tebes. Bani, borboleta no lalar poliniza kafé, ai-fuan no ai-horis fuik sira-nia ai-funan. Térmita, besouru no nehek halo ai-tahan no ai mate sai rai, no fó fali hahán ba rai. No insetu mak hahán ba manu, niki, teki, manduku no ikan. Espedisaun husi muzeu estranjeiru sira estuda ona insetu família balu iha Timór-Leste, no ema hotu bele ajuda: foti foto insetu no fahe iha plataforma siénsia sidadaun nian, hanesan iNaturalist.
text.pt: Os insetos têm seis patas e o corpo dividido em três partes: cabeça, tórax e abdómen. Muitos têm asas. São o grupo de animais com mais espécies do planeta, e em Timor-Leste ainda ninguém sabe quantas existem. Os seus papéis são essenciais. Abelhas, borboletas e moscas polinizam as flores do café, das árvores de fruto e das plantas selvagens. Térmitas, besouros e formigas desfazem folhas e madeira mortas e devolvem os nutrientes ao solo. E os insetos são comida para aves, morcegos, osgas, rãs e peixes. Expedições de museus estrangeiros já estudaram algumas famílias de insetos de Timor-Leste, e qualquer pessoa pode ajudar fotografando insetos e partilhando as fotos em plataformas de ciência cidadã, como o iNaturalist.
text.en: Insects have six legs and a body divided into three parts: head, thorax and abdomen. Many have wings. They are the group of animals with the most species on the planet, and in Timor-Leste nobody yet knows how many there are. Their roles are essential. Bees, butterflies and flies pollinate the flowers of coffee, fruit trees and wild plants. Termites, beetles and ants break down dead leaves and wood and return the nutrients to the soil. And insects are food for birds, bats, geckos, frogs and fish. Expeditions from foreign museums have already studied some families of insects in Timor-Leste, and anyone can help by photographing insects and sharing the photos on citizen-science platforms such as iNaturalist.
text.id: Serangga memiliki enam kaki dan tubuh yang terbagi menjadi tiga bagian: kepala, dada (toraks), dan perut (abdomen). Banyak serangga bersayap. Serangga adalah kelompok hewan dengan spesies terbanyak di planet ini, dan di Timor-Leste belum ada yang tahu berapa jumlahnya. Peran mereka sangat penting. Lebah, kupu-kupu, dan lalat menyerbuki bunga kopi, pohon buah, dan tumbuhan liar. Rayap, kumbang, dan semut menguraikan daun dan kayu mati serta mengembalikan zat hara ke tanah. Serangga juga menjadi makanan bagi burung, kelelawar, cicak, katak, dan ikan. Ekspedisi museum-museum asing sudah meneliti beberapa famili serangga di Timor-Leste, dan siapa pun dapat membantu dengan memotret serangga dan membagikan fotonya di platform sains warga seperti iNaturalist.

text.tet: Timór iha borboleta ne'ebé moris de'it iha illa ne'e. Ida ne'ebé furak liu mak Troides plato, borboleta liras-manu ida ne'ebé endémiku ba Timór, boot no ho liras kór-metan. Borboleta liras-manu nia ulat han ai-tali husi jéneru Aristolochia, tan ne'e borboleta ne'e moris de'it iha fatin ne'ebé iha ai-laran ho ai-horis sira-ne'e. Hanesan Troides hotu, konvensaun CITES proteje nia no kontrola ninia komérsiu internasionál. Borboleta seluk iha Timór mós endémiku, hanesan borboleta-tigre kinur ida husi jéneru Parantica no Delias oioin, borboleta ho kór barak; entomólogu ida husi Muzeu Austrália nota katak Delias barak liu iha Timór-Leste endémiku no raru iha koleksaun sira. Atu proteje borboleta, di'ak liu foti sira-nia foto duké kaer sira.
text.pt: Timor tem borboletas que só vivem na ilha. A mais vistosa é a Troides plato, uma borboleta-asa-de-pássaro endémica de Timor, grande e de asas escuras. As lagartas das borboletas-asa-de-pássaro comem trepadeiras do género Aristolochia, por isso esta borboleta só sobrevive onde há floresta com essas plantas. Como todas as Troides, está protegida pela convenção CITES, que controla o seu comércio internacional. Outras borboletas de Timor também são endémicas, como uma borboleta-tigre-amarela do género Parantica e várias Delias, borboletas muito coloridas; um entomólogo do Museu Australiano notou que a maioria das Delias de Timor-Leste é endémica e rara nas coleções. Para proteger as borboletas, é melhor fotografá-las do que apanhá-las.
text.en: Timor has butterflies that live only on the island. The most striking is Troides plato, a large, dark-winged birdwing butterfly endemic to Timor. Birdwing caterpillars eat climbing plants of the genus Aristolochia, so this butterfly survives only where there is forest with these plants. Like all Troides, it is protected by the CITES convention, which controls its international trade. Other butterflies of Timor are also endemic, such as a yellow tiger butterfly of the genus Parantica and several Delias, very colourful butterflies; an entomologist from the Australian Museum noted that most of the Delias of Timor-Leste are endemic and rare in collections. To protect butterflies, it is better to photograph them than to catch them.
text.id: Timor memiliki kupu-kupu yang hanya hidup di pulau ini. Yang paling mencolok adalah Troides plato, kupu-kupu sayap burung endemik Timor yang besar dan bersayap gelap. Ulat kupu-kupu sayap burung memakan tumbuhan merambat dari genus Aristolochia, sehingga kupu-kupu ini hanya dapat bertahan di tempat yang masih memiliki hutan dengan tumbuhan tersebut. Seperti semua Troides, kupu-kupu ini dilindungi oleh konvensi CITES, yang mengendalikan perdagangan internasionalnya. Kupu-kupu Timor lainnya juga endemik, seperti kupu-kupu harimau kuning dari genus Parantica dan beberapa Delias, kupu-kupu yang sangat berwarna-warni; seorang entomolog dari Museum Australia (Australian Museum) mencatat bahwa sebagian besar Delias di Timor-Leste endemik dan jarang ada dalam koleksi. Untuk melindungi kupu-kupu, lebih baik memotretnya daripada menangkapnya.

text.tet: Iha Tetun, abelha mak bani no mel mak bani-been. Iha Timór moris bani oioin ne'ebé fó bani-been. Bani boot (Apis dorsata) halo nia knuuk boot iha fatin nakloke, tara iha ai-hun aas ka fatuk sira. Iha Atauru, estudu ida husi 2019 to'o 2021 deskreve katak bainhira ai-hun barak moris ai-funan iha tempu hanesan, bani boot sira-nia grupu halo sira-nia knuuk, no tempu bani-been nian naruk liu fulan ida uitoan de'it kada tinan, ho kolleita baibain iha Abríl. Bani Ázia nian (Apis cerana) halo knuuk iha ai-kuak nia laran no ema bele hakiak nia iha kaixa, no bani ki'ik ne'ebé la tata fó bani-been ne'ebé siin liu. Ema ne'ebé foti bani-been ho di'ak uza ahi-suar ho kuidadu no husik knuuk nia parte ida atu bani sira moris nafatin. Sunu rai no pestisida oho bani sira.
text.pt: Em tétum, a abelha chama-se bani e o mel bani-been. Em Timor vivem várias abelhas que dão mel. A abelha-gigante (Apis dorsata) faz grandes favos ao ar livre, pendurados em árvores altas ou em rochas. Em Ataúro, um estudo feito entre 2019 e 2021 descreveu como os enxames destas abelhas fazem os seus ninhos quando muitas árvores florescem ao mesmo tempo, e como a época do mel dura pouco mais de um mês por ano, com a colheita em geral em abril. A abelha-asiática (Apis cerana) faz ninhos dentro de troncos ocos e pode ser criada em colmeias, e as pequenas abelhas sem ferrão dão um mel mais ácido. Um bom caçador de mel usa o fumo com cuidado e deixa parte do favo para a colónia sobreviver. As queimadas e os pesticidas matam as abelhas.
text.en: In Tetun, the bee is called bani and honey bani-been. Several kinds of honey-making bees live on Timor. The giant honey bee (Apis dorsata) builds large combs in the open, hanging from tall trees or rocks. On Ataúro, a study carried out between 2019 and 2021 described how swarms of these bees build their nests when many trees flower at the same time, and how the honey season lasts just over a month a year, with the harvest usually in April. The Asian honey bee (Apis cerana) nests inside hollow trunks and can be kept in hives, and the small stingless bees produce a more sour honey. A good honey hunter uses smoke carefully and leaves part of the comb so that the colony can survive. Burning and pesticides kill bees.
text.id: Dalam bahasa Tetun, lebah disebut bani dan madu disebut bani-been. Di Timor hidup beberapa jenis lebah penghasil madu. Lebah hutan (Apis dorsata) membuat sarang besar di tempat terbuka, menggantung di pohon tinggi atau di tebing batu. Di Ataúro, sebuah penelitian antara 2019 dan 2021 menggambarkan bagaimana kawanan lebah ini membuat sarang ketika banyak pohon berbunga bersamaan, dan bagaimana musim madu hanya berlangsung sedikit lebih dari sebulan setiap tahun, dengan panen biasanya pada bulan April. Lebah madu asia (Apis cerana) bersarang di dalam batang pohon yang berongga dan dapat dipelihara dalam stup (kotak sarang), sedangkan lebah kecil tanpa sengat menghasilkan madu yang lebih asam. Pemburu madu yang baik memakai asap dengan hati-hati dan menyisakan sebagian sarang agar koloninya dapat bertahan. Pembakaran lahan dan pestisida membunuh lebah.

heading.tet: Libélula, araña no kasadór ki'ik seluk
heading.pt: Libélulas, aranhas e outros pequenos caçadores
heading.en: Dragonflies, spiders and other small hunters
heading.id: Capung, laba-laba, dan pemburu kecil lainnya

text.tet: Animál ki'ik barak mak kasadór ne'ebé fó benefísiu. Libélula moris uluk iha bee laran, iha mota no natar, no depois semo atu kaer susuk no lalar; fatin ne'ebé iha libélula barak, baibain bee moos. Araña la'ós insetu: sira iha ain ualu no sira parte husi arakinídeu, hanesan eskorpiaun. Araña boot balu halo sira-nia rede kór-osan-mean iha ai-hun sira-nia leet, no kuaze araña hotu la halo aat ema. Maibé susuk bele hada'et moras: iha 2025, Organizasaun Mundiál Saúde (OMS) sertifika Timór-Leste livre husi malária, maibé dengue sei perigu nafatin. Atu prevene, hamamuk fatin hotu ne'ebé iha bee para, no toba iha kulambu nia okos. Molok hatais sapatu, baku sapatu uluk, tanba eskorpiaun no sentopeia bele tata.
text.pt: Muitos pequenos animais são caçadores úteis. As libélulas passam a primeira parte da vida dentro de água, nos rios e nos arrozais, e depois voam a caçar mosquitos e moscas; onde há muitas libélulas, a água costuma estar limpa. As aranhas não são insetos: têm oito patas e pertencem aos aracnídeos, como os escorpiões. Algumas aranhas grandes estendem teias douradas entre as árvores, e quase todas as aranhas são inofensivas para as pessoas. Já os mosquitos (susuk) podem transmitir doenças: em 2025, a Organização Mundial da Saúde certificou Timor-Leste como livre de malária, mas a dengue continua a ser um perigo. Para a evitar, deve-se esvaziar todos os recipientes com água parada e dormir debaixo de rede mosquiteira. Antes de calçar sapatos, convém sacudi-los, porque escorpiões e centopeias podem picar.
text.en: Many small animals are useful hunters. Dragonflies spend the first part of their lives in water, in rivers and rice fields, and then fly about hunting mosquitoes and flies; where there are many dragonflies, the water is usually clean. Spiders are not insects: they have eight legs and belong to the arachnids, like scorpions. Some big spiders spin golden webs between trees, and almost all spiders are harmless to people. Mosquitoes (susuk), on the other hand, can spread diseases: in 2025 the World Health Organization certified Timor-Leste as malaria-free, but dengue is still a danger. To avoid it, empty every container of standing water and sleep under a mosquito net. Before putting on shoes, it is wise to shake them out, because scorpions can sting and centipedes can bite.
text.id: Banyak hewan kecil adalah pemburu yang berguna. Capung menghabiskan bagian awal hidupnya di dalam air, di sungai dan sawah, lalu terbang memburu nyamuk dan lalat; di tempat yang banyak capungnya, airnya biasanya bersih. Laba-laba bukan serangga: laba-laba berkaki delapan dan termasuk araknida, seperti kalajengking. Beberapa laba-laba besar membentangkan jaring keemasan di antara pepohonan, dan hampir semua laba-laba tidak berbahaya bagi manusia. Sebaliknya, nyamuk (susuk) dapat menularkan penyakit: pada 2025 Organisasi Kesehatan Dunia (WHO) menyatakan Timor-Leste bebas malaria, tetapi demam berdarah masih menjadi bahaya. Untuk mencegahnya, kosongkan semua wadah yang berisi air tergenang dan tidurlah di bawah kelambu. Sebelum memakai sepatu, sebaiknya kibaskan dulu, karena kalajengking dapat menyengat dan lipan dapat menggigit.

heading.tet: Kadiuk no animál ki'ik tasi-ibun nian
heading.pt: Caranguejos e outros pequenos animais da costa
heading.en: Crabs and other small animals of the coast
heading.id: Kepiting dan hewan kecil lain di pesisir

text.tet: Kadiuk la'ós insetu, maibé sira família ho insetu: sira mós iha kulit-toos iha sira-nia isin li'ur no ain ho artikulasaun. Iha tasi-ibun, kadiuk-eremita moris iha kulit-tasi mamuk nia laran no troka kulit-tasi bainhira sira boot, no kadiuk-fantasma halai iha rai-henek iha loro-monu. Iha ai-parapa, kadiuk-violinista hasa'e sira-nia liman boot ida. Kadiuk balu ne'ebé moris iha rai hela iha kuak dook husi tasi, maibé sira-nia oan ki'ik moris uluk iha tasi. Kadiuk hamoos tasi-ibun no ai-parapa, no sai hahán ba manu no ikan, no família barak kaer sira atu han. Kaer de'it kadiuk boot, husik kadiuk feto ne'ebé lori tolun, no keta sobu ai-parapa: nune'e kadiuk sei iha ba futuru.
text.pt: Os caranguejos (kadiuk) não são insetos, mas são parentes deles: também têm o corpo protegido por uma carapaça e patas articuladas. Nas praias, os caranguejos-eremitas vivem dentro de conchas vazias e trocam de concha à medida que crescem, e os caranguejos-fantasma correm pela areia ao fim da tarde. Nos mangais, os caranguejos-violinistas acenam com uma pinça grande. Alguns caranguejos-terrestres vivem em buracos longe do mar, mas as suas larvas desenvolvem-se no mar. Os caranguejos limpam as praias e os mangais e alimentam aves e peixes, e muitas famílias apanham-nos para comer. Apanhar só os grandes, deixar as fêmeas com ovos e não destruir os mangais garante caranguejos para o futuro.
text.en: Crabs (kadiuk) are not insects, but they are related to them: they too have a body protected by a hard shell, and jointed legs. On the beaches, hermit crabs live inside empty shells and change shells as they grow, and ghost crabs run across the sand in the late afternoon. In the mangroves, fiddler crabs wave one big claw. Some land crabs live in burrows far from the sea, but their larvae develop in the sea. Crabs clean beaches and mangroves and are food for birds and fish, and many families catch them to eat. Catching only the big ones, leaving the females with eggs and not destroying the mangroves will make sure there are crabs in the future.
text.id: Kepiting (kadiuk) bukan serangga, tetapi masih berkerabat dengannya: tubuhnya juga dilindungi cangkang keras dan kakinya beruas-ruas. Di pantai, umang-umang hidup di dalam cangkang kosong dan berganti cangkang seiring pertumbuhannya, dan kepiting hantu berlarian di pasir pada sore hari. Di hutan bakau, kepiting biola melambaikan sebelah capitnya yang besar. Beberapa kepiting darat hidup di lubang yang jauh dari laut, tetapi larvanya berkembang di laut. Kepiting membersihkan pantai dan hutan bakau serta menjadi makanan bagi burung dan ikan, dan banyak keluarga menangkapnya untuk dimakan. Hanya menangkap kepiting yang besar, membiarkan betina yang sedang bertelur, dan tidak merusak hutan bakau akan menjamin adanya kepiting di masa depan.

summary.tet: IUCN nia Lista Mean klasifika ai-horis no animál sira tuir risku atu lakon. Iha Timór-Leste moris manu, lenuk, mamíferu no animál seluk ne'ebé iha perigu, hanesan kakatua ho fulun kinur iha ulun (Iha Perigu Boot Tebes) no pombu ai-fuan Timór nian (Iha Perigu).
